Conclusion: the live dispute is about what happened at Surabaya, and the people who saw it are there. Indonesia is arguably clearly more appropriate. Notice the method: write only the live factors, give each a direction and a weight, then conclude.

🎓 WHAT PROF CHONG SAID

Do not conflate stage 1 with the objective proper law test. Connections to the contract overlap, but witness compellability and where a patent is registered go to Spiliada only.

J4.1.3 Stage 2: substantial justice

▤ On your pre-write: J4.1.3 Stage 2: Substantial Justice (word for word)
J4.1.3 Stage 2: Substantial Justice

(justice balanced against comity; all circumstances count)

  • Threshold (−) Per Rotary, once [X] is clearly more appropriate, refusing a stay is "at least unusual"; [claimant] needs cogent evidence of a real and material risk of injustice in [X].
  • Real Risk, Cumulatively (+) Per AK Investment, a real risk in [this case] suffices, not proof that justice "will not" be done, and [several irregularities] may add up though none suffices alone (C&Y).
  • Comity (must write) (−) Per The Hung Vuong-2 and C&Y, the court is slow to impugn [X]'s courts, especially a well-established system (Shen Sophie: [US / China]), so generalised complaints about [X] fail.
  • Ordinary Differences (−) Per C&Y, ordinary differences in [procedure / remedies] are disregarded. Per Spiliada and Trendtex, [higher damages / discovery] here do not defeat a stay if substantial justice is available in [X].
  • Higher Damages (−) Presently [claimant] would recover [one third] of the Singapore award in [X]. Per Chong's feedback, a legitimate juridical advantage alone is not conclusive; per Goh Suan Hee, a likely higher award here was neutral, quantum's governing law being open.
  • Relief Unavailable (−) Per Rappo, [no constructive trust / tracing] in [X] is no injustice where [law X] governs, as it would be unavailable here too; per The Rainbow Joy, narrower remedies are not decisive.
  • Foreign Public Policy (±) Per Trisuryo, [X]'s public policy barring [the claim] is relevant but not determinative, rejecting the view that it is "a strong factor in favour of a stay".
  • Security Here (+) Per Spiliada, [claimant] keeps [its security] under a conditional stay.
  • Delay (−) Presently trial takes [5 years] in [X] against [10 months] here. Per C&Y, delay is disregarded unless egregious; per Grains and Industrial (and Chong's feedback), even alleged delays of [over 10 years in India] failed.
  • Funding and Legal Aid (±) Per Connelly v RTZ, [claimant] takes [X] as it finds it, so [no legal aid] alone fails, unless [the dispute] cannot be justly tried without [lawyers and experts] it cannot fund (Lubbe v Cape).
    • Illustration (+): per Chong (seminar), [no funding] counts only if [claimant] cannot pursue the claim in [X] at all, Singapore being less generous on legal aid. Similar to Limbu v Dyson (EWCA), where migrant workers at Malaysian factories, unable to fund suit there, sued the parent in England, [claimant] cannot fund [the action] in [X].
  • Time Bar (±) Per Spiliada, if [claimant] reasonably sued here and did not unreasonably let time run in [X], the stay is conditional on [defendant] waiving the bar. Presently [claimant] [was unaware / knowingly let time run], so the stay is [conditional / unconditional].
  • Time Bar: Limits (−) Per Chong's feedback, assert [claimant] is out of time in [X] only if the facts say so; parties often file [protective writs] in several fora. If only [some claims] are barred, the court is less willing to keep the case (C&Y; FLPA: J4.2.4).
  • Unfair Rules of Evidence (±) Per Rotary, system-wide rules like [discounting non-Muslim / female witnesses] can in principle ground injustice, but only if they prejudice [claimant] on the facts; cogent evidence is needed (Best Soar).
  • Instability (−) Per Shafeeg, [political unrest] in [X] is insufficient while its courts still function to try [the dispute].
  • Unfair Trial or Danger (+) [Cumulative irregularities] (AK Investment) or [risks of assassination / trumped-up charges] (Deripaska) suffice on cogent evidence, as does a system that "flies in the face of all accepted principles of justice" (Q & M v Poh Kiat).
  • No Trial Anywhere (+) Per AK Investment (applying Connelly v RTZ), where trial in [X] "never could" occur, justice favours Singapore; investing in [X] does not bind [claimant] to its courts.
  • Stay Is Suspensory (±) Per Rotary, where evidence of [arrest / danger] is thin, a stay goes, but [claimant] may lift it on fresh cogent evidence of exceptional circumstances striking at its basis, not as "a standing invitation".
  • Defendant's Stage 2 (±) If stage 1 fails, [defendant] may in principle show injustice in Singapore (IM Skaugen (HC)), e.g., [no legal aid or contingency funding for a foreign defendant], but it rarely succeeds (C&Y).

Once the foreign forum is clearly more appropriate, refusing a stay is "at least unusual" (Rotary). The claimant needs cogent evidence of a real and material risk of injustice, and the court is slow to criticise a foreign legal system (comity, "must write": The Hung Vuong-2).

Counts (+)Does not count (−)
Several irregularities adding up (AK Investment)Generalised complaints about the foreign system (comity)
Risk of assassination or trumped-up charges (Deripaska)Higher damages here alone (Chong; Goh Suan Hee)
A system that "flies in the face of all accepted principles of justice" (Q & M v Poh Kiat)Relief unavailable abroad where foreign law governs anyway (Rappo)
Trial abroad "never could" occur (AK Investment, applying Connelly)Delay unless egregious; political unrest while courts still function (Shafeeg)
Cannot fund the claim abroad at all (Lubbe v Cape; Per Chong (seminar), similar to Limbu v Dyson)No legal aid alone (Connelly v RTZ): take the forum as you find it
System-wide unfair evidence rules that prejudice the claimant on the facts (Rotary; Best Soar)Foreign public policy barring the claim is relevant but not determinative (Trisuryo)
🎓 WHAT PROF CHONG SAID

Say the claimant is out of time abroad only if the facts say so: parties often file protective writs in several places. And a stay is suspensory: if evidence of danger is thin, a stay goes, but the claimant may lift it on fresh cogent evidence, not as "a standing invitation" (Rotary).

✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Sorting the claimant's stage 2 complaints

Indonesia won stage 1. Alpha now says it would suffer injustice there. Sort each complaint:

Alpha's complaintCounts?
"Indonesian courts award lower damages."No. An ordinary difference between systems (Spiliada; Goh Suan Hee).
"Trial in Jakarta takes four years."No, unless egregious: even over 10 years in India failed (Grains and Industrial).
"Indonesian courts are generally unreliable." (a newspaper article)No. A generalised complaint; comity makes the court slow to criticise a foreign system (The Hung Vuong-2).
An expert report showing that in this case the court file was tampered with, a hearing was held without notice, and a witness was threatenedPossibly yes. Several concrete irregularities adding up, on cogent evidence (AK Investment).
"My claim is now time-barred in Indonesia."Only if Alpha reasonably sued here and did not unreasonably let time run abroad. Even then, the usual answer is a stay on condition that Beta waives the time bar (Spiliada).

The bar is high on purpose: Singapore will not refuse a stay just because the claimant prefers its own courts.

ℹ NOTE
J4.1.4 Evaluation: Spiliada v the Australian test

Australia stays only if it is a "clearly inappropriate forum" (Voth; Puttick v Tenon). Singapore rejected this (JIO; Eng Liat Kiang). Per C&Y, Spiliada is more consonant with comity at stage 1 but its stage 2 judges the foreign court, which Voth avoids. The tests diverge only where the foreign forum is more appropriate but Singapore is not clearly inappropriate.

4J4.2 Forum conveniens on service out

▤ On your pre-write: J4.2.1 Burden and Standard (word for word)
J4.2.1 Burden and Standard
  • Mirror Image (must write) Per Zoom, forum conveniens (service out) and forum non conveniens (stay) are one Spiliada test with the burden reversed: [claimant] shows Singapore is more appropriate; on a stay, [defendant] shows [X] is. It goes only to PD para 63(2)(b), not a free-standing discretion.
  • Burden Stays on Claimant Per Spiliada, Oriental Insurance and Zoom, [claimant] bears it without notice and still when [defendant] sets aside, jurisdiction over [a foreign defendant] being "an imposition" on it (Li Shengwu).
  • Not Merely Equal (−) [Defendant] argues Singapore is at most one of several equal fora. Per Sudarga, that fails: [claimant] must show Singapore is the more appropriate forum, with the most real and substantial connection (Oro Negro).
  • How Much More (±) Per Spiliada, AK Investment and Zoom, [claimant] must show Singapore "clearly" more appropriate than [X]; per Oro Negro (adopting Siemens), "on balance" suffices, "by a hair or by a mile". Cite "clearly", flag Oro Negro, argue [both].
  • Asymmetry Deliberate On a stay, [defendant] must show [X] clearly or distinctly more appropriate (JIO; CIMB), protecting jurisdiction as of right. JIO's relativity answers [defendant]'s better-forum point; it does not let [claimant] rest on parity.
  • Quality Not Quantity Per Oro Negro (following JIO and Rappo), [claimant] cannot win by counting [connecting factors]; their weight against [the issues in dispute] decides.

Per Zoom, forum conveniens (service out) and forum non conveniens (stay) are one Spiliada test with the burden reversed. On service out, the claimant must show Singapore is the more appropriate forum.

PointStay after service inService out
Who bears stage 1DefendantClaimant, without notice and on the set-aside (Zoom; Li Shengwu)
How much more appropriateThe foreign forum clearly or distinctly more appropriate (JIO; CIMB)Singapore "clearly" more appropriate (Spiliada; AK Investment), or "on balance" (Oro Negro, adopting Siemens). Cite both.
Equal foraNo stayFails: Singapore must be the more appropriate forum, not one of several equal ones (Sudarga)
Why the asymmetryProtects jurisdiction founded as of rightJurisdiction over a foreign defendant is "an imposition" on it (Li Shengwu)
✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Same scales, different starting weight

Picture the court's scales with Singapore on one side and Indonesia on the other. The factors (witnesses, law, place of performance) are the same in both procedures. What changes is which way the scales must tip.

  • Stay (Beta served in Singapore): the scales must tip clearly towards Indonesia, or Alpha keeps its case here. A level balance means no stay.
  • Service out (Beta served in Indonesia): the scales must tip towards Singapore, or Alpha loses its case here. A level balance means Alpha fails (Sudarga).

So with perfectly balanced factors, the result flips depending on how Beta was served. That is why claimants prefer service in (J2.0).

▤ On your pre-write: J4.2.3 Stage 2 After Service Out (word for word)
J4.2.3 Stage 2 After Service Out
  • Claimant Wins Stage 1 (±) Per IM Skaugen (HC), [defendant] may still show it would suffer injustice here. Confine this to [procedural differences, e.g., broader disclosure in X], not aspersions on Singapore's courts.
  • Merits No Answer (+) That [defendant] would win in [X] but lose here goes to the merits. Per Vinmar and Chong (seminar), the court does not engage with the merits at the jurisdictional stage, so [claimant] will probably keep [the case].
  • Claimant Fails Stage 1: Second Bite? (must write) Presently [the factors point to X], so can [claimant] still show injustice there? Per Oro Negro and IM Skaugen (CA), this is open: Lewis v King and Metall for; Konamaneni and Fentiman against.
  • Against (−) Per Konamaneni, [claimant] failing stage 1 "is the end of the matter"; per Allenger, running stage 2 would confer jurisdiction over [defendant] where none was established.
  • For: Spiliada Itself (+) Spiliada was a service-out case: England was not the natural forum, yet leave was granted because [the claim] was time-barred in [Canada]. Lord Goff also weighed [defendant]'s residence and [the gateway invoked].
  • For: Principle (+) Per Shen Sophie (adopting Yeo) and C&Y, access to justice and even-handed treatment of [claimant] and [defendant] apply both ways, both bases rest on statute, and O 8 was meant to expand [extraterritorial jurisdiction].
  • Konamaneni's Fallback (+) Even on the narrow view, injustice in [X] may make it not "available" at stage 1, though the SGCA prefers [fair-trial points] at stage 2. On Spiliada's framing, "appropriate forum" is the conclusion after stage 2.
  • Substance (±) Run J4.1.3. E.g., [an allegation that X's courts favour state-linked parties like defendant] needs cogent evidence (AK Investment) and is risky: if it fails, [the case] goes to [X] with the allegation on record.
Time bars and the FLPA
▤ J4.2.4
  1. 1Common law: a foreign rule extinguishing the right was substantive; one barring the remedy procedural, so a claimant could be out of time abroad but in time here: a classic stage 2 argument.
  2. 2FLPA s 3(1): where foreign law governs, its limitation law applies, not Singapore's. s 3(2): in tort, the lex loci delicti's period, or that of the single law chosen under the flexible exception (C3).
  3. 3s 4(2): the foreign period is disapplied only for "undue hardship" caused by the bar itself (Recovery Vehicle 1).
  4. 4Effect: if every court applies the lex causae's period, the bar follows the claimant everywhere, so time bars recede at stage 2.
✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Why the FLPA shrinks the time-bar argument

A contract is governed by Ruritanian law, which gives two years to sue. Singapore's own period would be longer. Alpha waits three years, then sues in Singapore and argues: "If you stay this case, I'm out of time in Ruritania, so I'd suffer injustice."

Under the FLPA, the Singapore court would also apply the Ruritanian two-year period, because Ruritanian law governs (s 3(1)). Alpha is out of time here too. Staying the case takes nothing away from Alpha, so there is no stage 2 injustice. Only "undue hardship" caused by the bar itself could disapply the foreign period (s 4(2); Recovery Vehicle 1).

ℹ NOTE
J4.2.5 Parallel proceedings and strategy

There is no first-seised rule (unlike Brussels' "Italian torpedo"): each court decides for itself. A foreign ruling that it is the natural forum does not estop Singapore (Lakshmi). A defendant served out should argue forum within its set-aside, where the claimant bears the burden; a separate stay on the same material is "wholly unnecessary and likely counter-productive" (Zoom).

5J4.3 Strong cause

▤ On your pre-write: J4.3.0 Starter (must write) (word for word)
J4.3.0 Starter (must write)

Presently, [claimant] sues here in breach of [the EJC for X] / [defendant] seeks a stay or set-aside in breach of [the Singapore EJC / NEJC]. Per Vinmar (restating The Eleftheria), the court holds the parties to their bargain unless [the party in breach] shows strong cause, whether on a stay or a set-aside (Shanghai Turbo).

🎓 WHAT PROF CHONG SAID

Never call Spiliada "the strong cause test". Strong cause applies only where someone broke the clause; Spiliada where no one did.

★ IN PLAIN ENGLISH

Spiliada asks "where is the best place for this case?" Strong cause asks "is there a strong enough reason to let you break your word?" Those are very different questions. If you booked a venue a year ago, "it's raining today" or "my friends live far away" are not good reasons to cancel: you knew the weather and the distance when you booked. Only something you could not have foreseen, or something that makes the booked venue truly useless, will do.

J4.3.1 Why it is harder than Spiliada

  • Party autonomy and certainty. "It should take more" to keep the case from the chosen court, since the court is asked to sanction a breach (Vinmar).
  • Foreseeable factors (witnesses abroad, foreign law, the chosen court's delays) carry little weight: the parties knew them when they contracted (Vinmar; Shanghai Turbo).
  • Singapore NEJC: strong cause means the same thing (Shanghai Turbo: witnesses, documents and residence in China, plus related Chinese proceedings, were insufficient).
  • Two grounds where only the clause's parties are involved: abuse of process or denial of justice. With non-parties, fragmentation may suffice. The list is not closed.

J4.3.2 The Eleftheria factors (as restated in Vinmar)

▤ On your pre-write: J4.3.2 The Eleftheria Factors (as restated in Vinmar) (word for word)
J4.3.2 The Eleftheria Factors (as restated in Vinmar)
  • (a)–(c) Connections Where [the evidence] is and the relative cost of trial in [Singapore / X]; whether [law X] applies and differs materially; how closely [each party] is connected with [X]. Usually foreseeable, so rarely enough alone.
  • (d) Abuse; (e) Prejudice (d) whether [the applicant] is acting abusively; (e) whether [claimant] would be prejudiced in [X] by losing [security], being unable to [enforce], facing [a time bar], or getting no fair trial for [political / racial / religious] reasons.
  • Flip for a Singapore Clause Framed for a suit here in breach of [a foreign EJC]. Where [defendant] objects to [a Singapore EJC / NEJC], keep (a)–(c) but flip (d) and (e): [claimant]'s seising is abusive, or [defendant] would be prejudiced defending here (Shanghai Turbo; Vinmar).
  • Caution on Flipped (e) Like a defendant's Spiliada stage 2, this tells a Singapore judge Singapore is unjust, so confine it to [concrete, cogently evidenced prejudice] to [defendant].
  • Foreseeable Prejudice Per Chong's mid-term comments, that [the claim] is time-barred in [X] but alive under [Singapore's longer period] is arguably no prejudice to [defendant], which agreed to Singapore's jurisdiction and so foresaw its time limits.
  • Enforcing a Singapore Judgment Per C&Y, that [a Singapore judgment] may not be enforced where [defendant's assets] are was foreseeable, so weighs little; (e)(ii) concerns [claimant]'s inability to enforce [X's judgment].
The Eleftheria checklist
▤ J4.3.2. (a)–(c) are usually foreseeable, so rarely enough alone.
  1. 1(a) Where the evidence is, and the relative cost of trial.
  2. 2(b) Whether foreign law applies and differs materially.
  3. 3(c) How closely each party is connected with each country.
  4. 4(d) Whether the applicant is acting abusively (very high threshold).
  5. 5(e) Whether the claimant would be prejudiced abroad: losing security, unable to enforce, a time bar, no fair trial for political, racial or religious reasons.
⚠ TRAP
Flip (d) and (e) for a Singapore clause

The factors were framed for a suit here in breach of a foreign clause. Where the defendant objects to a Singapore clause, keep (a)–(c) but flip (d) and (e): is the claimant's seising abusive, or would the defendant be prejudiced defending here? Confine flipped (e) to concrete, cogently evidenced prejudice. Per Chong's mid-term comments, a claim time-barred abroad but alive under Singapore's longer period is arguably no prejudice to the defendant, who agreed to Singapore and foresaw its time limits.

J4.3.3 Abuse and denial of justice

▤ On your pre-write: J4.3.3 Abuse of Process and Denial of Justice (word for word)
J4.3.3 Abuse of Process and Denial of Justice
  • Merits Irrelevant (must write) [Claimant] argues [defendant] has no genuine defence. Per Vinmar, overruling The Jian He, that is not entertained: parties choose [forum X] to "win or lose" there, whatever the merits.
  • Why Per Vinmar, a merits inquiry breeds [uncertainty, cost and delay]; the merits are irrelevant to FNC, IAA stays and ASIs; and seeking [the agreed forum's procedural advantages, e.g., its interest or costs rules] is legitimate.
  • Abuse Reformulated Per Vinmar, (d) asks whether [the applicant] is acting abusively, a very high threshold, e.g., [defendant] [admits liability and quantum but cannot pay / runs a media campaign in X to taint the trial]. Euromark (treating (d) as irrelevant) was not followed.
  • Chosen Court Unavailable Per Vinmar, strong cause exists where [X's chosen court] is dissolved or unavailable through [war], or trial there would be so overwhelmingly difficult as to deny justice, if unforeseeable; notorious delay in [X] is foreseeable and insufficient.
  • No Remedy at All Per Trisuryo, strong cause was shown because [Indonesian law] would not recognise [the trust over Indonesian shares], so [claimant] could get no remedy in [X]. It was exceptional, and [foreign illegality] goes to the merits, not the stay.
  • Time Bar Per Vinmar, a bar in [X] counts only if [claimant] shows "very good reasons" for not filing [a protective writ] there; otherwise it is self-induced.
  • Merits are irrelevant ("must write"). Per Vinmar, overruling The Jian He, "no genuine defence" is not entertained: parties choose a forum to "win or lose" there.
  • Abuse reformulated. Very high threshold: e.g. the defendant admits liability and quantum but cannot pay, or runs a media campaign abroad to taint the trial (Vinmar; Euromark not followed).
  • Chosen court unavailable: dissolved, or war, or trial so overwhelmingly difficult as to deny justice, if unforeseeable. Notorious delay is foreseeable and insufficient.
  • No remedy at all. In Trisuryo, Indonesian law would not recognise the trust over Indonesian shares, so the claimant could get no remedy there: strong cause shown. Exceptional.
  • Time bar abroad counts only with "very good reasons" for not filing a protective writ there; otherwise self-induced.
✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Strong cause on a claimant who sued in breach

A clause gives the Tokyo courts exclusive jurisdiction. Alpha sues Nippon KK in Singapore anyway. Nippon seeks a stay, so Alpha must show strong cause. Run the Eleftheria factors:

  1. (a) Evidence and cost: Alpha's witnesses are in Singapore. Foreseeable when Alpha signed: little weight.
  2. (b) Law: Singapore law governs, so a Tokyo court would need it proved. Foreseeable: little weight.
  3. (c) Connections: Alpha is a Singapore company. Foreseeable.
  4. (d) Abuse: Nippon does not admit the debt, so this is not the "admits liability but cannot pay" case. Alpha's real point is that Nippon "has no genuine defence", but per Vinmar the merits are irrelevant.
  5. (e) Prejudice abroad: Alpha says it is now time-barred in Japan. That counts only if Alpha had very good reasons for not filing a protective claim there; otherwise the problem is self-induced.

Result: Alpha is held to its bargain, and the Singapore action is stayed. Compare the same facts under Spiliada: Alpha's points might have carried real weight, because there would be no promise to hold it to.

J4.3.4 Fragmentation and standard forms

▤ On your pre-write: J4.3.4 Fragmentation and Standard Forms (word for word)
J4.3.4 Fragmentation and Standard Forms
  • Fragmentation (±) Per Vinmar (citing Donohue), where [non-parties] are involved, splitting [the dispute] across [Singapore and X] risks duplication, inconsistent findings and a race to judgment, and may be strong cause, unless foreseeable at contracting.
  • Limited Overlap Per Shanghai Turbo, related [foreign proceedings] with [different parties / causes of action / remedies] are not strong cause.
  • Counterweight Per Hive Marketing, a stay of [the related claims] is discretionary, not presumptive, merely because [multiplicity / inconsistent decisions] may follow; otherwise the court paints with "too broad and indiscriminate a brush" (CSFB v MLC).
  • Use Both Ways Plead it against [the party in breach] invoking fragmentation (the foreseeable price of [clause X]), and against [the party] resisting a stay on multiplicity alone. The one-stop rationale belongs to scope (J1.5), fragmentation being "a fact of life" (COSCO (CA)).
  • CCAA Contrast Per 6DM, [the risk that a related party cannot be joined in X] might be strong cause at common law but falls far short of s 12(1)(c) manifest injustice under [an HCCCA clause] (J1.4).
  • Standard Form Contracts (±) [The bill of lading] was not negotiated. Per Vinmar (tentatively; ZI Pompey), strong cause still applies for consistency, though autonomy is weaker; [consumers / employees] are better protected by forum mandatory rules. Shanghai Turbo left this open for NEJCs.
  • Fragmentation with non-parties (duplication, inconsistent findings, race to judgment) may be strong cause unless foreseeable (Vinmar, citing Donohue). Related foreign proceedings with different parties, causes or remedies are not (Shanghai Turbo). A stay of related claims is discretionary, not presumptive (Hive Marketing).
  • CCAA contrast. The inability to join a related party might be strong cause at common law but falls far short of s 12(1)(c) manifest injustice (6DM; J1.4).
  • Standard forms. Per Vinmar (tentatively), strong cause still applies to a bill of lading for consistency; consumers and employees are better protected by forum mandatory rules. Shanghai Turbo left this open for NEJCs.
✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
When fragmentation might be enough

A Hong Kong EJC binds only Alpha and Beta. Alpha's loss was caused jointly by Beta and by two Singapore companies, C and D, which signed nothing. Alpha sues all three in Singapore. Beta seeks a stay.

If Beta's part goes to Hong Kong while C and D are sued here, the same facts are tried twice, with a risk of inconsistent findings and a race to judgment. If Alpha could not have foreseen C and D's involvement when it agreed to the clause, that fragmentation may be strong cause (Vinmar, citing Donohue).

But if the related foreign proceedings simply involve different parties, causes or remedies, that is not enough (Shanghai Turbo). And in a CCAA case, the same argument fails s 12(1)(c) outright (6DM).

✍ EXAM-READY SENTENCES
Strong cause, Singapore NEJC

Delta's application to set aside service objects to Singapore in breach of cl 18, so per Shanghai Turbo it must show strong cause (Vinmar). Its reliance on witnesses and documents in China and on related Chinese proceedings fails: those factors were foreseeable when it agreed to cl 18, and the Chinese proceedings involve different parties and remedies. Delta does not allege abuse or denial of justice, so it is held to its bargain.

6J4.4 The SICC factor

▤ On your pre-write: J4.4 THE SICC FACTOR IN THE GENERAL DIVISION'S SPILIADA ANALYSIS (word for word)
J4.4 THE SICC FACTOR IN THE GENERAL DIVISION'S SPILIADA ANALYSIS (insert at J4.1.2 / J4.2)
  • Relevant (+) Presently, [claimant] resists [a stay / shows forum conveniens] by pointing to possible transfer to the SICC. Per Rappo, the court must not "shut its eyes" to [foreign law on submissions (s 18L) / international judges].
  • Internal Allocation Per Rappo (citing Yeo) and C&Y, transferring [the action] to the SICC is a later question of internal allocation (J5.4), and there must be no "unprincipled jurisdictional grab" for [the dispute].
  • Burden on Claimant (−) Per Rappo, the SICC is not "a free pass": [claimant] must name [the particular SICC feature] and show [the dispute] suits it, with the transfer requirements prima facie met; absent a prima facie international and commercial case, no weight.
  • Never Decisive (−) Per IM Skaugen, the judge erred in letting [the SICC factor] tip [a German-law, German-tort fraud claim] to Singapore; alone it cannot displace [State B], which "would virtually always" be the forum.
  • At Most a Discount (±) Per IM Skaugen, it discounts the weight of [law B], depending on similarity to Singapore law and complexity. Presently [law B] is [a similar common law system / civil law with complex issues], so the discount is [significant / slight].

In IM Skaugen, the judge erred in letting the SICC factor tip a German-law, German-tort fraud claim to Singapore: alone it cannot displace the foreign forum. How big the discount is depends on how similar the foreign law is to Singapore law and how complex the issues are.

★ IN PLAIN ENGLISH

Normally, "this dispute is governed by German law" pulls towards Germany, because German judges know German law and a Singapore court would need experts to prove it. The SICC can soften that pull: foreign law can be argued on submissions there (s 18L), and it has international judges. So the SICC factor works like a discount coupon on the foreign-law factor. It makes that factor lighter. It never adds a new weight of its own on Singapore's side of the scales.

7J4.5 Overlays: parallel proceedings

▤ On your pre-write: J4.5 OVERLAYS: LIS ALIBI PENDENS, LIMITED STAY AND FORUM ELECTION (word for word)
J4.5 OVERLAYS: LIS ALIBI PENDENS, LIMITED STAY AND FORUM ELECTION
  • Three Routes Where [the dispute] is also pending in [X], [defendant] may rely on it at stage 1 (J4.1.2), seek a limited stay, or make a common claimant elect; it is no bar here, unlike the EU first-seised rule.
  • Limited Stay Per Rappo and 6DM, the court may stay [the Singapore action / part of it] pending [X's jurisdiction ruling / the related proceedings], managing [fragmentation risk] at an early stage.
  • Forum Election: Common Claimant Per Koh Kay Yew and Virsagi, where [claimant] sues [defendant] here and in [X] on [the same issues], it must elect unless it justifies the multiplicity, to "prevent the inherent abuse" of different judicial systems.
  • Case Management Only Per Rappo, election never fixes the trial forum: if [claimant] elects Singapore, [defendant] may still seek an FNC stay; if it elects [X], the action here is stayed and [defendant] may seek an ASI (Koh Kay Yew; J6).
    • Exception: unless [defendant] accepts [claimant]'s choice or made [a representation] that [claimant] relied on (Rappo).
  • FNC First Per Rappo, where [defendant] runs both, FNC is decided first, and election follows only if [X] is not clearly more appropriate, saving [resources] and following logic (C&Y).
  • Different Parties or Issues Election does not apply to [related proceedings] with different parties or issues, or where [defendant] sues in [X] (reversed parties); these go to FNC (J4.1.2) or an ASI (J6).
  • Limited stay. The court may stay the Singapore action, or part of it, pending the foreign jurisdiction ruling or related proceedings (Rappo; 6DM).
  • Election never fixes the trial forum. If the claimant elects Singapore, the defendant may still seek an FNC stay; if it elects the foreign forum, the action here is stayed (Rappo), unless the defendant accepted the choice or made a representation the claimant relied on.
✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Suing in two places at once

Alpha sues Beta in both Singapore and Kuala Lumpur over the same unpaid invoices.

  1. FNC first. Beta asks for a stay. If Malaysia is clearly more appropriate, the Singapore action is stayed under Spiliada and the election question never arises (Rappo).
  2. Then election. If Malaysia is not clearly more appropriate, Alpha is the claimant in both places, so it must elect one, unless it can justify running both (Koh Kay Yew; Virsagi).
  3. Different picture: if instead Beta had started the KL case, there is no election. The KL case is a stage 1 factor, or a reason for a limited stay, or a target for an ASI (J6).

8Put it together: two worked stays

✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Hypo 1: no clause

Alpha (Singapore) sues Beta, an Indonesian company registered in Singapore and served at its Singapore registered office (s 376 CA), for fraudulent misrepresentations made in Jakarta and relied on there. Indonesian law governs. Beta seeks a stay.

  1. Test (J4.0.2): no clause, served in, so Spiliada with stage 1 on Beta.
  2. Available: Indonesian courts have jurisdiction over Beta.
  3. Stage 1 (J4.1.2): the tort was committed in Indonesia (prima facie the natural forum, JIO), Indonesian law governs and witnesses are there. Indonesia is clearly more appropriate.
  4. Stage 2 (J4.1.3): Alpha says trial in Jakarta takes years and damages are lower. Neither suffices without cogent evidence of egregious delay (Grains and Industrial). Stay granted.
✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Hypo 2: a Singapore EJC

Same facts, but the contract has "the courts of Singapore shall have exclusive jurisdiction". Beta seeks a stay.

  1. Test: Beta objects to the chosen forum, so strong cause on Beta (J4.3).
  2. Eleftheria (flipped): witnesses and Indonesian law were foreseeable. Beta alleges no abuse by Alpha and no concrete prejudice in defending here.
  3. Result: Beta is held to its bargain. No stay. (And if the CCAA applied, s 11 would require Singapore to hear the case anyway: J1.3.)
